home.introHeadline: I grew up under Oklahoma skies and grew into myself under New York Lights.
home.introBody: Hi y'all! My name is Hannah Jew. A multi-hyphenate artist based in New York City and telling stories that don't fit in one box. It all started back in my hometown of Oklahoma, separation anxiety almost got the best of me and I'm not quite sure why it was that random day, but after several attempts to stay in the studio without crying, I did and have not looked back ever since. I think it was meant to be that I was going to be a dancer/artist. I love everything about the arts: the process, what happens behind the scenes and the magic onstage. I'm always excited to meet new people and experience new things. As I continue to evolve as a person and artist, I'm so excited to see all the unexpected and beautiful experiences that are yet to come. Maybe you'll be a stepping stone in my journey too! And I'm grateful to have so many people that are Click below to learn more about me and thank you for the support!

paragraphs: Hi y'all! My name is Hannah Jew, an Asian American multi-hyphenate artist based in New York City and telling stories that don't fit in one box. My love of dance started back in my hometown of Oklahoma City, OK, but it started off a little rocky. Although I loved dancing at home, it was a bit of a different story when I first stepped foot in ballet class. I like to tell this story for the next child who has trouble making it into a class due to separation anxiety. I guess it was meant to be because after many tries (and Mom not giving up on me, thanks Mom!), I went into the studio and never looked back. Dance allowed me to pursue my passion as a career and has taken me into different fields of the arts, hence the multi-hyphenate now. I'm always looking forward to the many more stepping stones in my journey to learn and to grow. Thank you for the support and following along in my journey.

about.lead: Hannah Jew (周健倫) (She/Her) is a New York City based multi-hyphenate artist, educator and frequent collaborator with other creative disciplines.
paragraphs: Born and raised in Oklahoma, Hannah's love of dance began at Classical Ballet School in Oklahoma City, OK. She later joined Oklahoma City Ballet as an apprentice before earning her BFA in Ballet Performance from The University of Oklahoma. She spent summers training with Complexions Contemporary Ballet, Joffrey Ballet, American Ballet Theatre, San Francisco Ballet and Tulsa Ballet.

Hannah has danced with Nai-Ni Chen Dance Company, Ballet Hispánico (BHdos), Dayton Ballet and Oklahoma City Ballet. She then went on to join The King and I National Tour (dir. Bartlett Sher, chor. Christopher Gattelli). Hannah's recent favorite credits include dancing in Alexandra Light's "Nightmare Screen" at Dallas Indie Dance Festival (TX) and Uptown Rising (NY) in which the piece won "Audience Favorite," being a featured dancer in AES Indiana Yuletide Celebration, Eliza in The King and I (Beef & Boards Dinner Theatre - Indianapolis, IN),performing with the New York City Opera and dancing at New York Fashion Week.

Being able to bring Asian representation in the arts is very important to Hannah and she has been able to do that through dancing at The Museum of Chinese in America (NY) in "Quiet Acts of Becoming" (chor. Shan Chuang), choreographing/dancing in "Year of the Rabbit" with the Chinese Music Ensemble of New York at the China Institute, being a part of readings with the Museum of Chinese in America (NY), Pan Asian Repertory Theatre (NY), New York Theatre Workshop (NY) and PlayGround SF.

As a choreographer, Hannah returned to her alma mater (The University of Oklahoma) to recreate the Chinese divertissement (now called "Ribbon Dance") to eliminate racial stereotypes in which it premiered with Oklahoma Festival Ballet in Norman, OK and then on tour to Colorado Springs, CO. She has choreographed/danced in a collaboration with Chengjin Koh (composer) and Verona Quartet in "Mountain of Echoing Halls," - a world premiere at the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art (Washington, D.C.) and created a new work titled, "Lai See (Red Envelope Blessings)" for the students of Booker T. Washington High School for the Performing and Visual Arts (Dallas, TX).

As an educator, Hannah is currently on faculty at Circle in the Square Theatre School (NY) and teaches dance to all ages and levels, including individuals with disabilities in which while she was with Nai-Ni Chen Dance Company received the Innovator Award at the Excellence in Cultural Access Awards for Project D.R.E.AM. with her colleagues in New Jersey for creating a dance program for the students of A. Harry Moore School (Jersey City, NJ). She has taught master classes at The University of Oklahoma, Booker T. Washington High School for the Performing and Visual Arts (Dallas, TX) and Dance Clinic GBI (Freeport, Bahamas).
She is a member of Actors' Equity Association and is represented by Clear Talent Group.
She spends her downtime exploring local coffee shops, reading, following NBA games/cheering on her favorite teams, lifting weights and snacking on sour candy!
